# Spark UI (@sparkwire)

> React component library with a "Live Wire" look: components carry current (sparks on press, flowing current on hover, a lever switch with a bulb). Accessible behaviour from React Aria, zero-runtime CSS with --spark-* variables, light/dark/system modes, works in React Server Components. Use it as an npm package (@sparkwire/core) or copy the source (npx sparkwire add <name>).

Key facts for writing code:
- Import the stylesheet once: import '@sparkwire/core/styles.css'. Set the mode with data-spark-theme="dark" | "light" | "system" on <html> or any wrapper.
- App-wide defaults and slot classes: <SparkProvider components={{ Button: { defaultProps: { variant: 'outlined' } } }} locale="hi-IN">.
- Every component takes className, and most take classNames for inner parts. State is exposed as data-* attributes (data-state, data-open, data-invalid, data-disabled) for CSS or Tailwind.
- Forms: inputs take name and work with FormData and React Hook Form. Dropdown/Combobox/Slider/DatePicker submit through hidden inputs.
- Dates are plain JS Date objects; DatePicker submits ISO YYYY-MM-DD. Locales and calendar systems (indian, islamic-umalqura, buddhist...) are supported.
- Pick a value: Dropdown (alias Select). Search then pick: Combobox. Run actions: Menu.
- Custom markup with Spark behaviour: useSwitch, useCheckbox, useSlider, useDatePicker, useSpark from '@sparkwire/core/headless'. Building blocks: ButtonBase, InputBase, Popover, ListBox, Overlay from '@sparkwire/core/base'.
- The npm scope is @sparkwire (not @spark-ui, which is a different library).

## Button (`button`)
Throws sparks from the press point; current runs along outlined buttons on hover.

```tsx
import { Button } from '@sparkwire/core';
```
Install: `npx sparkwire add button` (copy source) or use the npm package. Examples and props: https://phoenix-am.github.io/spark-ui/components/button

### Button
The button you'll reach for most. It handles clicks, keyboard presses and
focus the way people expect, comes in three weights (contained, outlined,
text) and four colours, and throws a little burst of sparks from wherever
it's pressed. Need a link that looks like a button? Render it as one with
`as` or `render`.

Throws sparks from the press point. Outlined and text buttons show
current flowing along a wire on hover; a disabled button is a dead circuit.
Built on ButtonBase; forwards `ref` to the rendered element.

- `as?`: `ElementType` Render as another element or component, e.g. `"a"` or a router Link.
- `children?`: `ReactNode` The label. Keep it short and say what happens: “Save changes”, not “OK”.
- `className?`: `string` Extra class names for the outermost element.
- `classNames?`: `Partial<Record<"root" | "icon", string>>` Extra classes for each part: root, icon.
- `color?`: `ButtonColor` Tone of the current. Default `brand`.
- `disabled?`: `boolean` Dead circuit: no clicks, no sparks, dashed outline.
- `disableElevation?`: `boolean` Remove the glow around contained buttons.
- `endIcon?`: `ReactNode` Icon after the label. Coloured with the text.
- `fullWidth?`: `boolean` Stretch to the container's width.
- `href?`: `string` Use with `as="a"` to render a link that looks like a button.
- `render?`: `RenderProp<{ disabled: boolean; }>` Render a different element with the button's behaviour and look, e.g. `render={<Link href="/pricing" />}`.
- `size?`: `ButtonSize` Height 36, 44 or 52px. Default `medium`.
- `spark?`: `boolean` Throw sparks from the press point on click. Default `true`.
- `startIcon?`: `ReactNode` Icon before the label. Coloured with the text.
- `variant?`: `ButtonVariant` `contained` (filled, default), `outlined` or `text`.
- `ripple?`: `boolean` **Deprecated.** Use `spark`. Kept so existing code keeps working.

## Spark (`spark`)
A burst of sparks from a point; used by Button and Calendar.

```tsx
import { Spark } from '@sparkwire/core';
```
Install: `npx sparkwire add spark` (copy source) or use the npm package. Examples and props: https://phoenix-am.github.io/spark-ui/components/spark

### Spark
The burst of sparks behind Sparkwire's buttons, available on its own. Drop
it inside anything clickable and fire it from the pointer for a moment of
delight on the actions that matter. It quietly does nothing for people who
prefer reduced motion.

The signature Live Wire effect. Place it inside a `position: relative`
element and call `burst()` from its click handler. Renders nothing for users
who prefer reduced motion.

- `colors?`: `string[]` Particle colours. Defaults to the theme's `--spark-energy-spark-1…3`.
- `count?`: `number` (default `10`) Particles per burst. Default 10.
- `duration?`: `number` (default `700`) Burst duration in milliseconds. Default 700.
- `spread?`: `number` (default `70`) How far particles travel, in px. Default 70.

## Switch (`switch`)
A lever switch that lights a bulb.

```tsx
import { Switch } from '@sparkwire/core';
```
Install: `npx sparkwire add switch` (copy source) or use the npm package. Examples and props: https://phoenix-am.github.io/spark-ui/components/switch

### Switch
An on/off control for settings that take effect straight away, like
notifications or dark mode. It reads as a real switch to screen readers,
flips with Space, and can show a small bulb that lights up when it's on.

A lever that closes a circuit. When on, current lights the wire and
the bulb; when off, the lever lifts and the circuit goes dark.

Style hooks: `.sp-switch`, `[data-state="on"|"off"]`, and the parts
`.sp-switch__node`, `__wire`, `__lever`, `__bulb`, `__label`.

- `aria-label?`: `string` Defines a string value that labels the current element.
- `aria-labelledby?`: `string` Identifies the element (or elements) that labels the current element.
- `checked?`: `boolean` Controlled state.
- `classNames?`: `Partial<Record<"label" | "root" | "control" | "node" | "wire" | "lever" | "bulb", string>>` Extra classes for each part: root, control, node, wire, lever, bulb, label.
- `color?`: `Tone` Colour of the current when on. Default `brand`.
- `defaultChecked?`: `boolean` Initial state when uncontrolled.
- `label?`: `ReactNode` Visible label. Use `aria-label` instead when there is none.
- `name?`: `string` Form field name. When set, a hidden input submits `value` while the switch is on.
- `onChange?`: `((checked: boolean, event: MouseEvent<HTMLButtonElement, MouseEvent>) => void)` Called with the new state when the user flips the switch.
- `showBulb?`: `boolean` Show the bulb that lights when the circuit is closed. Default `true`.
- `size?`: `"small" | "medium" | "large"` Default `medium`.
- `value?`: `string` Value submitted with `name` while on. Default `"on"`.
- `wrapperClassName?`: `string` Class for the outer wrapper (the button gets `className`).

## Checkbox (`checkbox`)
A checkbox that closes a circuit.

```tsx
import { Checkbox } from '@sparkwire/core';
```
Install: `npx sparkwire add checkbox` (copy source) or use the npm package. Examples and props: https://phoenix-am.github.io/spark-ui/components/checkbox

### Checkbox
For yes-or-no choices and for picking several items from a list. It supports
an indeterminate state for “some selected”, sits nicely in forms, and shows
errors with a message rather than colour alone.

A terminal. Checking it powers the terminal: it fills with current
and the tick is drawn in. Built on a native checkbox, so forms and keyboards work.

Style hooks: `.sp-checkbox`, `__box`, `__label`, `__helper`; the native input
drives `:checked`, `:indeterminate` and `:disabled`.

- `aria-label?`: `string` Defines a string value that labels the current element.
- `aria-labelledby?`: `string` Identifies the element (or elements) that labels the current element.
- `classNames?`: `Partial<Record<"label" | "root" | "box" | "helper", string>>` Extra classes for each part: root, box, label, helper.
- `color?`: `Tone` Colour when checked. Default `brand`.
- `error?`: `boolean` Marks the checkbox invalid and colours it with the error tone.
- `helperText?`: `ReactNode` Help or error text under the label.
- `indeterminate?`: `boolean` Shows a dash: some, but not all, of a group is selected.
- `label?`: `ReactNode` Text next to the box.
- `size?`: `"small" | "medium" | "large"` Default `medium`.

## RadioGroup (`radio-group`)
One live wire at a time.

```tsx
import { RadioGroup } from '@sparkwire/core';
```
Install: `npx sparkwire add radio-group` (copy source) or use the npm package. Examples and props: https://phoenix-am.github.io/spark-ui/components/radio-group

### RadioGroup
Pick exactly one option from a short list where it helps to see every choice
at once. Show options as a simple list, or as cards with room for a
description, which works well for plans and regions.

A selector switch. Every option is a contact; only the chosen one
carries current, so its core lights up. Native radios underneath, so arrow
keys and forms work as expected.

Style hooks: `.sp-radio-group`, `__option[data-checked]`, `__dot`, `__text`.

- `label`: `ReactNode` The group's legend. Required for accessibility.
- `options`: `RadioOption[]` The choices, each `{ value, label, description?, disabled? }`.
- `className?`: `string` Extra class names for the outermost element.
- `color?`: `Tone` Colour of the chosen contact. Default `brand`.
- `defaultValue?`: `string` Initial value when uncontrolled.
- `error?`: `boolean` Marks the group invalid.
- `helperText?`: `ReactNode` Help or error text under the group.
- `name?`: `string` Form field name. Generated when omitted.
- `onChange?`: `((value: string) => void)` Called with the newly selected option's `value`.
- `value?`: `string` Controlled value.
- `variant?`: `"list" | "cards"` `list` stacks options; `cards` lays them out as selectable cards.

## Slider (`slider`)
A dimmer, with two-knob ranges.

```tsx
import { Slider } from '@sparkwire/core';
```
Install: `npx sparkwire add slider` (copy source) or use the npm package. Examples and props: https://phoenix-am.github.io/spark-ui/components/slider

### Slider
Choose a number by dragging, or a range with two thumbs. Values are
formatted with Intl, so prices, percentages and units read naturally, and
the arrow keys give precise control.

A dimmer. The wire is lit up to the knob, and the glow gets stronger
the higher you turn it. Pass a `[start, end]` value for a range: current
flows between two knobs. Behaviour comes from React Aria: arrows, Page
Up/Down, Home/End, dragging, clicking the track, right-to-left, and
localized numbers. Each knob holds a native range input, so forms and
React Hook Form's `register` work.

Style hooks: `.sp-slider[data-range][data-disabled]`, `__header`, `__value`,
`__track`, `__fill`, `__thumb[data-dragging][data-focus-visible]`.
Variables: `--sp-start`, `--sp-end` and `--sp-pct` (0–100).

- `aria-label?`: `string` Defines a string value that labels the current element.
- `aria-labelledby?`: `string` Identifies the element (or elements) that labels the current element.
- `classNames?`: `Partial<Record<"value" | "label" | "root" | "header" | "track" | "fill" | "thumb", string>>` Extra classes for each part: root, header, label, value, track, fill, thumb.
- `color?`: `Tone` Default `brand`.
- `defaultValue?`: `SliderValue` Initial value when uncontrolled. A `[start, end]` pair makes it a range. Defaults to `min`.
- `formatOptions?`: `NumberFormatOptions` Intl number options when `formatValue` isn't set, e.g. `{ style: 'currency', currency: 'INR' }`.
- `formatValue?`: `((value: number) => string)` Format each value for the label and for screen readers.
- `label?`: `ReactNode` Visible label, shown with the current value.
- `max?`: `number` Default 100.
- `min?`: `number` Default 0.
- `name?`: `string | [string, string]` Form field name. For a range, one name (sent twice) or `[startName, endName]`.
- `onChange?`: `((value: T) => void)` Called on every move with the new value (a number, or `[start, end]`).
- `onChangeEnd?`: `((value: T) => void)` Called once when the user lets go, e.g. to save or fetch.
- `ref?`: `Ref<HTMLInputElement>` Ref to the hidden range input, for form libraries that need direct access.
- `step?`: `number` Default 1.
- `thumbLabels?`: `[string, string]` Screen-reader names for the two knobs of a range. Default `['Minimum', 'Maximum']`.
- `value?`: `SliderValue` Controlled value: a number, or `[start, end]` for a range with two knobs.

## Textfield (`textfield`)
A field that charges as you type.

```tsx
import { Textfield } from '@sparkwire/core';
```
Install: `npx sparkwire add textfield` (copy source) or use the npm package. Examples and props: https://phoenix-am.github.io/spark-ui/components/textfield

### Textfield
A text input with a label, helper text and error state built in. It also has
a party trick: a charge meter that fills up as the value gets more complete,
handy for password strength or profile progress.

In Live Wire, a field can "charge up" as its value becomes valid.
Pass `charge` (0..1, or a function of the value) to show the meter.

Style hooks: `.sp-textfield` with `[data-focused]`, `[data-invalid]`,
`[data-charged]`, `[data-disabled]`; parts `__label`, `__control`, `__input`,
`__adornment`, `__meter`, `__helper`. Built on InputBase (`.sp-input-base`).

- `append?`: `ReactNode` Content at the end of the input, like a unit (“kg”) or an icon button.
- `aria-label?`: `string` Defines a string value that labels the current element.
- `aria-labelledby?`: `string` Identifies the element (or elements) that labels the current element.
- `cardDetection?`: `((value: string) => string)` Function that names the card network from the number typed, e.g. returns “Visa”; shown inside the field.
- `charge?`: `number | ((value: string) => number)` Live Wire charge meter. A number from 0 to 1, or a function that maps the current value to 0..1 (e.g. password strength). At 1 the field is fully charged and current runs along the meter.
- `chargeLabel?`: `((percent: number) => ReactNode)` Text announced next to the meter. Receives the charge as 0..100.
- `classNames?`: `Partial<Record<"label" | "root" | "control" | "input" | "adornment" | "meter" | "helper", string>>` Extra classes for each part: root, label, control, input, adornment, meter, helper.
- `containerStyle?`: `CSSProperties` Inline styles for the wrapper around the label, input and helper text.
- `defaultValue?`: `string` Initial value when uncontrolled (no `value`). Works with React Hook Form's `register`.
- `disabled?`: `boolean` Turns the control off: it can't be focused or changed, and it's announced as disabled.
- `error?`: `boolean` Shows the field in its error state. Pair it with `helperText` explaining what to fix.
- `formatPhoneNumber?`: `((value: string) => string)` Function that formats the value as it's typed, e.g. `98765 43210`.
- `helperText?`: `string` Short guidance under the field. Shown in red with an error.
- `inputSize?`: `"small" | "medium" | "large"` Height and text size of the input. Default `medium`.
- `isCurrency?`: `boolean` Formats the value as money while typing (thousand separators, two decimals).
- `label?`: `string` Visible label, linked to the input.
- `onBlur?`: `((event: FocusEvent<HTMLInputElement, Element>) => void)` Called when the field loses focus. Handy for validating on blur.
- `onChange?`: `((event: ChangeEvent<HTMLInputElement>) => void)` Called on every keystroke with the change event; read `event.target.value`.
- `onFocus?`: `((event: FocusEvent<HTMLInputElement, Element>) => void)` Called when the field gains focus.
- `placeholder?`: `string` Hint shown while the field is empty. Don't use it instead of a label; it disappears as soon as someone types.
- `prepend?`: `ReactNode` Content at the start of the input, like a currency symbol or a search icon.
- `type?`: `"hidden" | "color" | "button" | "checkbox" | "date" | "datetime-local" | "email" | "file" | "image" | "month" | "password" | "radio" | "range" | "reset" | "search" | "submit" | ... 8 more ...` The kind of input, like `email`, `password` or `tel`. It sets the mobile keyboard and browser autofill. Default `text`.
- `value?`: `string` The current text, when you control the field yourself. Use `defaultValue` to let it manage its own state.
- `variant?`: `"outlined" | "filled" | "standard"` `outlined` (default) draws a full border, `filled` a tinted background, `standard` just an underline.

## Field (`field`)
Label, help text and error wiring for any control.

```tsx
import { Field } from '@sparkwire/core';
```
Install: `npx sparkwire add field` (copy source) or use the npm package. Examples and props: https://phoenix-am.github.io/spark-ui/components/field

### Field
Turns any control into a proper form field. Give it a label, a description
and an error, wrap your input, and Field connects them all for screen
readers so you don't have to juggle ids.

Label, help text and error for any control, wired for screen readers.
Use it to give your own inputs (a textarea, a third-party editor) the same
labelling and error handling as Spark UI's built-in fields.

Style hooks: `.sp-field[data-invalid][data-disabled]`, `__label`,
`__required`, `__description`, `__error`.

- `children`: `ReactElement<any, string | JSXElementConstructor<any>> | ((props: FieldControlProps) => ReactNode)` One element (ids and aria props are added to it), or a function that receives the props to spread: `{(p) => <textarea {...p} />}`.
- `label`: `ReactNode` Visible label, linked to the control.
- `className?`: `string` Extra class names for the field wrapper.
- `classNames?`: `Partial<Record<"root" | "label" | "description" | "error", string>>` Extra classes for each part: root, label, description, error.
- `description?`: `ReactNode` Help text under the control.
- `disabled?`: `boolean` Dims the label and passes `disabled` to the input inside.
- `error?`: `ReactNode` Error message. Replaces the description and marks the control invalid.
- `id?`: `string` Control id. Generated when omitted.
- `required?`: `boolean` Adds a required marker and `required` on the control.

## NumberField (`number-field`)
Locale-formatted numbers (₹1,00,000, %, units) with steppers.

```tsx
import { NumberField } from '@sparkwire/core';
```
Install: `npx sparkwire add number-field` (copy source) or use the npm package. Examples and props: https://phoenix-am.github.io/spark-ui/components/number-field

### NumberField
For numbers people type rather than drag: quantities, budgets, percentages.
It formats as you go (₹25,000, 15%), keeps values inside min and max, and
steps with buttons, arrow keys or the scroll wheel.

A number input that formats as you'd write it in your
language (₹1,00,000 in India, 
00,000 in the US, 15 %, 2.5 kg). Up/Down
and the − / + buttons step; Page Up/Down step by tens; Home/End jump to
min/max; values are clamped and snapped to `step` on blur. Built on React
Aria's number field and the InputBase base component.

Style hooks: `.sp-number-field[data-invalid][data-disabled]`, `__label`,
`__stepper`, `__helper`; the field is `.sp-input-base`.

- `aria-label?`: `string` Accessible name, read by screen readers. Use it when there's no visible label.
- `className?`: `string` Extra class names for the outermost element.
- `classNames?`: `Partial<Record<"root" | "label" | "field" | "input" | "stepper" | "helper", string>>` Extra classes for each part: root, label, field, input, stepper, helper.
- `defaultValue?`: `number | null` Starting value when the field manages its own state. Use `null` to start empty.
- `disabled?`: `boolean` Turns the control off: it can't be focused or changed, and it's announced as disabled.
- `error?`: `ReactNode` An error message, or `true` to mark the field invalid and show `helperText` as the error.
- `formatOptions?`: `NumberFormatOptions` How the number looks, in the user's locale: `{ style: 'currency', currency: 'INR' }`, `{ style: 'percent' }`, `{ style: 'unit', unit: 'kilogram' }`, `{ maximumFractionDigits: 2 }`…
- `helperText?`: `ReactNode` Help text under the field (shown in the error colour when `error` is `true`).
- `hideSteppers?`: `boolean` Hide the − / + buttons.
- `label?`: `string` Visible label. Use `aria-label` instead if there is no visible label.
- `max?`: `number` Largest allowed value. Typing more snaps back to it, and the + button stops.
- `min?`: `number` Smallest allowed value. Typing less snaps back to it, and the − button stops.
- `name?`: `string` Form field name; submits the plain number (e.g. 100000, not "₹1,00,000").
- `onChange?`: `((value: number) => void)` Called with the parsed number (or NaN when cleared) as the value commits.
- `placeholder?`: `string` Hint shown while the field is empty.
- `readOnly?`: `boolean` Shows the value but doesn't allow changes. Unlike `disabled`, it can still be focused and copied.
- `required?`: `boolean` Marks the field as required: screen readers announce it and the form won't submit while it's empty.
- `size?`: `"small" | "medium" | "large"` Default `medium`.
- `startIcon?`: `ReactNode` Icon shown at the start of the field.
- `step?`: `number` Step for the buttons and arrow keys. Default 1.
- `value?`: `number | null` Controlled value; `null` when empty.

## ToggleGroup (`toggle-group`)
Segmented control or a row of independent toggles, with arrow-key navigation.

```tsx
import { ToggleGroup, ToggleGroup.Item, ToggleGroupItem } from '@sparkwire/core';
```
Install: `npx sparkwire add toggle-group` (copy source) or use the npm package. Examples and props: https://phoenix-am.github.io/spark-ui/components/toggle-group

### ToggleGroup
A row of buttons that act as one control. Use it as a segmented switch
between views, or let several be on at once, like bold and italic in a
toolbar. Arrow keys move between options.

A row of related toggle buttons, as a segmented control
(`single`) or independent toggles (`multiple`). Arrow keys move between
items, one Tab stop for the group; selected items have `aria-checked` /
`aria-pressed`.

```tsx
<ToggleGroup aria-label="View" defaultValue="grid">
  <ToggleGroup.Item value="list">List</ToggleGroup.Item>
  <ToggleGroup.Item value="grid">Grid</ToggleGroup.Item>
</ToggleGroup>
```

Style hooks: `.sp-toggle-group[data-variant][data-size]`, `__item[data-selected]`.

- `children`: `ReactNode` The options: one `ToggleGroupItem` each.
- `allowEmpty?`: `boolean` In `single` mode, allow clicking the selected item to clear it. Default `false`.
- `aria-label?`: `string` Accessible name, read by screen readers. Use it when there's no visible label.
- `aria-labelledby?`: `string` Id of an element whose text names this component, instead of `aria-label`.
- `className?`: `string` Extra class names for the outermost element.
- `classNames?`: `Partial<Record<"root" | "item", string>>` Extra class names for the component's inner parts, keyed by part name. Handy with Tailwind.
- `defaultValue?`: `string | string[] | null` Starting selection when the group manages its own state: one value, or an array with `selectionMode="multiple"`.
- `disabled?`: `boolean` Turns the control off: it can't be focused or changed, and it's announced as disabled.
- `fullWidth?`: `boolean` Stretch to fill the width.
- `onChange?`: `((value: M extends "multiple" ? string[] : string | null) => void)` Called with the new selection: a value (or `null`), or an array of values in multiple mode.
- `orientation?`: `"horizontal" | "vertical"` Lay the options out in a row (`horizontal`, default) or a column. Arrow keys follow the direction.
- `selectionMode?`: `Mode` `single` (default): one at a time, like a segmented control. `multiple`: each toggles on its own (bold / italic / underline).
- `size?`: `"small" | "medium" | "large"` Height and text size. Default `medium`.
- `value?`: `string | string[] | null` Selected value(s): a string for `single`, a string[] for `multiple`.
- `variant?`: `"segmented" | "outlined"` `segmented` (default): one track with a sliding fill. `outlined`: separate buttons.

### ToggleGroup.Item
One option inside a ToggleGroup. Give it a value and a label, or an icon
with an `aria-label`.

- `value`: `string` Identifies this option in the group's `value` and `onChange`.
- `aria-label?`: `string` Accessible name for an option that shows only an icon.
- `children?`: `ReactNode` The option's label.
- `className?`: `string` Extra class names for this option's button.
- `disabled?`: `boolean` Makes just this option unavailable.
- `icon?`: `ReactNode` Icon before the label. For icon-only items, pass `aria-label`.

### ToggleGroupItem
One option inside a ToggleGroup. Give it a value and a label, or an icon
with an `aria-label`.

- `value`: `string` Identifies this option in the group's `value` and `onChange`.
- `aria-label?`: `string` Accessible name for an option that shows only an icon.
- `children?`: `ReactNode` The option's label.
- `className?`: `string` Extra class names for this option's button.
- `disabled?`: `boolean` Makes just this option unavailable.
- `icon?`: `ReactNode` Icon before the label. For icon-only items, pass `aria-label`.

## Stepper (`stepper`)
Progress through a multi-step flow; clickable steps, errors, vertical, compact on small screens.

```tsx
import { Stepper } from '@sparkwire/core';
```
Install: `npx sparkwire add stepper` (copy source) or use the npm package. Examples and props: https://phoenix-am.github.io/spark-ui/components/stepper

### Stepper
Stepper: progress through a multi-step flow (checkout, onboarding,
forms). Finished steps show a check, the current one is lit with flowing
current between steps, and failed ones show an error. Optionally
clickable to go back. An ordered list with `aria-current="step"`; status
is spelled out for screen readers, never colour alone.

Style hooks: `.sp-stepper[data-orientation]`, `__step[data-status]`, `__indicator`, `__connector[data-done]`.

- `active`: `number` Index of the current step (0-based). Steps before it are complete.
- `steps`: `StepItem[]` The steps in order, each `{ label, description?, error?, icon? }`.
- `aria-label?`: `string` Accessible name, read by screen readers. Use it when there's no visible label.
- `className?`: `string` Extra class names for the outermost element.
- `classNames?`: `Partial<Record<"root" | "step" | "indicator" | "label" | "description" | "connector", string>>` Extra class names for the component's inner parts, keyed by part name. Handy with Tailwind.
- `clickable?`: `"completed" | "all"` Let people jump back to a step by clicking it. `completed` (default when `onStepClick` is set): finished steps only. `all`: any step (non-linear).
- `onStepClick?`: `((index: number) => void)` Called with a step's index when it's clicked. Setting it makes steps clickable (see `clickable`).
- `orientation?`: `"horizontal" | "vertical"` Steps in a row (`horizontal`, default) or a column, which leaves room for descriptions.
- `responsive?`: `boolean` Under ~480px a horizontal stepper shows "Step 2 of 4 · Label". Default `true`.

## FileUpload (`file-upload`)
Drop zone and file list with type/size/count checks, thumbnails, progress and errors.

```tsx
import { FileUpload } from '@sparkwire/core';
```
Install: `npx sparkwire add file-upload` (copy source) or use the npm package. Examples and props: https://phoenix-am.github.io/spark-ui/components/file-upload

### FileUpload
Drag and drop or browse for files, with type and size limits checked as
files arrive. Rejected files come with a clear reason, images can show
previews, and everything works from the keyboard.

Drop files on the zone or browse. Checks type, size and count
before accepting, lists files with thumbnails, progress and errors, and
lets people remove them. Uploading is yours: start it in `onAdd`, then
feed `progress` / `status` back through `files`.

The zone is a real button (keyboard and screen readers), and drag-and-drop
uses React Aria's `useDrop`, which also accepts keyboard and screen-reader drops.

Style hooks: `.sp-file-upload`, `__zone[data-drop-target][data-invalid]`, `__item[data-status]`, `__progress`.

- `accept?`: `string` Like the input attribute: "image/*,.pdf".
- `className?`: `string` Extra class names for the outermost element.
- `classNames?`: `Partial<Record<"root" | "label" | "zone" | "list" | "item" | "errors", string>>` Extra class names for the component's inner parts, keyed by part name. Handy with Tailwind.
- `defaultFiles?`: `UploadFile[]` Files to show at the start, like ones already uploaded.
- `disabled?`: `boolean` Turns the control off: it can't be focused or changed, and it's announced as disabled.
- `files?`: `UploadFile[]` Files in the list (controlled). Update `progress` / `status` as uploads run.
- `hint?`: `ReactNode` Line under the main prompt. Default lists accepted types and size.
- `label?`: `ReactNode` Label above the drop zone.
- `maxFiles?`: `number` Most files allowed. Extra files are turned away with a message.
- `maxSize?`: `number` Bytes.
- `multiple?`: `boolean` Allow choosing more than one file.
- `name?`: `string` Submit the files with a regular form.
- `onAdd?`: `((added: UploadFile[]) => void)` Just the newly accepted files: start uploads here.
- `onChange?`: `((files: UploadFile[]) => void)` Whole list after adding or removing.
- `onReject?`: `((rejected: FileRejection[]) => void)` Files that failed `accept`, `maxSize` or `maxFiles`. Default messages are shown under the zone.
- `onRemove?`: `((file: UploadFile) => void)` Called with a file when someone removes it from the list.
- `previews?`: `boolean` Image thumbnails in the list. Default `true`.
- `prompt?`: `ReactNode` Main prompt. Default "Drop files here or browse".

## TimePicker (`time-picker`)
Type a time segment by segment or pick from suggestions every N minutes; min/max and blocked slots.

```tsx
import { TimePicker } from '@sparkwire/core';
```
Install: `npx sparkwire add time-picker` (copy source) or use the npm package. Examples and props: https://phoenix-am.github.io/spark-ui/components/time-picker

### TimePicker
Enter a time by typing, using the arrow keys on each part, or picking from a
list. It respects 12 and 24-hour clocks for the locale and can limit choices
to business hours or fixed steps.

Type a time segment by segment (hours, minutes, AM/PM), or
pick from a list of suggestions every `step` minutes. Values are plain
24-hour strings ("14:30"), so they store and submit cleanly; the field
shows the locale's format. `min`, `max` and `isTimeDisabled` limit both
typing and the list.

Built on React Aria's `useTimeField` with the same segments as DatePicker,
and the Popover and ListBox base components.

Style hooks: shares `.sp-date-picker` styles; `.sp-time-picker`, `__list`, `__option[data-disabled]`.

- `aria-label?`: `string` Accessible name, read by screen readers. Use it when there's no visible label.
- `className?`: `string` Extra class names for the outermost element.
- `classNames?`: `Partial<Record<"root" | "label" | "control" | "field" | "trigger" | "helper" | "popover" | "list", string>>` Extra class names for the component's inner parts, keyed by part name. Handy with Tailwind.
- `clearable?`: `boolean` Show a button that empties the field.
- `defaultValue?`: `string | null` Starting time when the picker manages its own state, as `"HH:mm"` (24-hour), e.g. `"09:30"`.
- `disabled?`: `boolean` Turns the control off: it can't be focused or changed, and it's announced as disabled.
- `error?`: `boolean` Shows the field in its error state. Pair it with `helperText` explaining what to fix.
- `granularity?`: `"hour" | "minute" | "second"` `minute` (default) or `second`.
- `helperText?`: `ReactNode` Short guidance under the field. Shown in red with an error.
- `hourCycle?`: `12 | 24` 12 or 24-hour. Default: the locale's.
- `isTimeDisabled?`: `((time: string) => boolean)` Grey out suggestions, e.g. booked slots: `(t) => booked.includes(t)`.
- `label?`: `ReactNode` Visible label above the field.
- `max?`: `string` Latest time, "HH:mm".
- `min?`: `string` Earliest time, "HH:mm".
- `name?`: `string` Submits "HH:mm" with forms.
- `onChange?`: `((value: string | null) => void)` Called with the new time as `"HH:mm"`, or `null` when cleared.
- `required?`: `boolean` Marks the field as required: screen readers announce it and the form won't submit while it's empty.
- `showList?`: `boolean` Turn off the suggestion list (typing only).
- `size?`: `"small" | "medium" | "large"` Height and text size. Default `medium`.
- `step?`: `number` Minutes between suggestions in the list. Default 30.
- `value?`: `string | null` "HH:mm" or "HH:mm:ss", 24-hour. `null` when empty.

## Textarea (`textarea`)
Multi-line text that grows with its content, with a character count.

```tsx
import { Textarea } from '@sparkwire/core';
```
Install: `npx sparkwire add textarea` (copy source) or use the npm package. Examples and props: https://phoenix-am.github.io/spark-ui/components/textarea

### Textarea
Multi-line text with the niceties built in: it can grow with its content,
show a live character count, and display errors next to the field.

Multi-line text on the same shell as every other field
(`.sp-input-base`). Grows with its content (`autoResize`), can show a
character count, and links its label, help text and error for screen
readers.

Style hooks: `.sp-textarea[data-invalid]`, `__label`, `__input`, `__helper`, `__count[data-over]`.

- `aria-label?`: `string` Defines a string value that labels the current element.
- `aria-labelledby?`: `string` Identifies the element (or elements) that labels the current element.
- `autoResize?`: `boolean` Grow with the content between `minRows` and `maxRows`. Default `true`.
- `classNames?`: `Partial<Record<"label" | "root" | "field" | "input" | "helper" | "count", string>>` Extra class names for the component's inner parts, keyed by part name. Handy with Tailwind.
- `error?`: `string | boolean` `true` marks it invalid; a string also replaces the helper text.
- `helperText?`: `ReactNode` Help text under the field.
- `label?`: `ReactNode` Visible label above the text area.
- `maxRows?`: `number` Default 10; beyond this it scrolls.
- `minRows?`: `number` Default 3.
- `onChange?`: `((value: string, event: ChangeEvent<HTMLTextAreaElement>) => void)` Called with the new text and the change event on every keystroke.
- `showCount?`: `boolean` Show "12 / 280" under the field. Uses `maxLength` when set.
- `variant?`: `"outlined" | "filled" | "standard"` `outlined` (default), `filled` or `standard`.

## Alert (`alert`)
Info, success, warning and error messages, with actions, dismiss and a banner variant.

```tsx
import { Alert } from '@sparkwire/core';
```
Install: `npx sparkwire add alert` (copy source) or use the npm package. Examples and props: https://phoenix-am.github.io/spark-ui/components/alert

### Alert
A message that sits in the page: a heads-up, a success, a warning or an
error. Errors are announced to screen readers immediately; the rest wait
politely. Add an action or let people dismiss it.

A message about the page or a task — info, success, warning or
error — with an icon, optional title, actions and a dismiss button. Use
`variant="banner"` for a site-wide strip. Errors are announced at once;
others are static unless you set `live`.

Style hooks: `.sp-alert[data-tone][data-variant]`, `__icon`, `__title`, `__body`, `__action`, `__dismiss`.

- `action?`: `ReactNode` Buttons or links on the right (or below on narrow screens).
- `aria-label?`: `string` Defines a string value that labels the current element.
- `aria-labelledby?`: `string` Identifies the element (or elements) that labels the current element.
- `children?`: `ReactNode` The message itself. One or two sentences works best.
- `classNames?`: `Partial<Record<"title" | "root" | "icon" | "body" | "action" | "dismiss", string>>` Extra class names for the component's inner parts, keyed by part name. Handy with Tailwind.
- `dismissLabel?`: `string` Accessible name for the close button. Default “Dismiss”, translated with the locale.
- `icon?`: `ReactNode` Replace the tone icon, or `false` to hide it.
- `live?`: `"polite" | "assertive" | "off"` `polite` announces it when it appears, `assertive` interrupts (errors). Default: `assertive` for error, otherwise none (static content).
- `onDismiss?`: `(() => void)` Show a close button. Called after it hides.
- `render?`: `RenderProp<{ tone: AlertTone; }>` Render any element as the root, e.g. a `section` with your own landmark.
- `title?`: `ReactNode` Bold headline above the message.
- `tone?`: `AlertTone` Default `info`. Each tone ships with its own icon, so meaning is never colour alone.
- `variant?`: `"soft" | "outlined" | "banner"` `soft` (default), `outlined`, or `banner` (full-width, square, for the top of a page).

## Navigation (`navigation`)
Breadcrumbs and Pagination.

```tsx
import { Breadcrumbs, Pagination } from '@sparkwire/core';
```
Install: `npx sparkwire add navigation` (copy source) or use the npm package. Examples and props: https://phoenix-am.github.io/spark-ui/components/breadcrumbs

### Breadcrumbs
A trail that shows where a page sits in your app and offers a quick way back
up. Long trails collapse in the middle so they never wrap awkwardly.

Where this page sits. The last item is the current page
(`aria-current="page"`); long trails collapse in the middle with
`maxItems`. Works with any router through `renderLink`.

Style hooks: `.sp-breadcrumbs`, `__item`, `__link`, `__current`, `__separator`, `__ellipsis`.

- `items`: `BreadcrumbItem[]` The trail from the top level down, each `{ label, href?, icon? }`. Leave `href` off the last item, the current page.
- `aria-label?`: `string` Accessible name, read by screen readers. Use it when there's no visible label.
- `className?`: `string` Extra class names for the outermost element.
- `classNames?`: `Partial<Record<"root" | "item" | "link" | "current" | "separator", string>>` Extra class names for the component's inner parts, keyed by part name. Handy with Tailwind.
- `maxItems?`: `number` Show at most this many; the middle collapses to "…". Default: all.
- `renderLink?`: `((props: { href: string; className: string; children: ReactNode; }) => ReactNode)` Render links with your router, e.g. `({ href, ...p }) => <Link href={href} {...p} />`.
- `separator?`: `ReactNode` Default "/"-style chevron.

### Pagination
Page numbers with sensible gaps, so twelve pages or twelve hundred both fit.
There's a compact version for tight spots like table footers, and it can
render real links for server-rendered pages.

Move between pages of results. Previous/next, page numbers
with ellipses (1 … 4 5 6 … 20), the current page marked
`aria-current="page"`, and real links when `getHref` is given.
`variant="compact"` shows "Page 3 of 12" for tight spaces.

Style hooks: `.sp-pagination[data-size]`, `__item[aria-current]`, `__ellipsis`, `__summary`.

- `count`: `number` Total pages.
- `aria-label?`: `string` Accessible name, read by screen readers. Use it when there's no visible label.
- `boundaries?`: `number` Pages always shown at each end. Default 1.
- `className?`: `string` Extra class names for the outermost element.
- `classNames?`: `Partial<Record<"root" | "item" | "ellipsis" | "summary", string>>` Extra class names for the component's inner parts, keyed by part name. Handy with Tailwind.
- `defaultPage?`: `number` Starting page (1-based) when the component manages its own state.
- `disabled?`: `boolean` Turns the control off: it can't be focused or changed, and it's announced as disabled.
- `getHref?`: `((page: number) => string)` Build an href per page to render real links (good for SEO and new tabs).
- `labels?`: `{ previous?: string; next?: string; page?: ((n: number) => string) | undefined; of?: ((page: number, count: number) => string) | undefined; } | undefined` Labels for translation.
- `onChange?`: `((page: number) => void)` Called with the newly chosen page number.
- `page?`: `number` Current page, 1-based.
- `siblings?`: `number` Pages shown on each side of the current one. Default 1.
- `size?`: `"small" | "medium"` Height and text size. Default `medium`.
- `variant?`: `"pages" | "compact"` `pages` (default) or `compact` ("Page 3 of 12" with arrows, for small screens).

## Charts (`charts`)
Our own SVG charts: Line/Area, Bar (grouped, stacked, horizontal), Donut, Sparkline. Validated colour-blind-safe palette, tooltips, keyboard, data-table view.

```tsx
import { LineChart, BarChart, DonutChart, Sparkline } from '@sparkwire/core';
```
Install: `npx sparkwire add charts` (copy source) or use the npm package. Examples and props: https://phoenix-am.github.io/spark-ui/components/line-chart

### LineChart
Show how something changes over time. Hover, or focus the chart and use the
arrow keys, to read exact values. Fill the area underneath, stack series,
and switch to a data table view for screen readers.

Change over time or an
ordered axis. Thin 2px lines that draw in like current, a crosshair and
tooltip that follow the pointer, keyboard stepping (focus the chart, then
← →), legend toggles, and a data-table view. One y axis only.

Style hooks: `.sp-chart[data-kind="line"|"area"]`, `__line`, `__area`,
`__crosshair`, `__point`, `__grid`, `__axis`. Colours: `--spark-chart-1…8`.

- `data`: `Row[]` One object per point on the x axis, with a field for `x` and one for each series, e.g. `{ month: 'Jan', sales: 420 }`.
- `series`: `ChartSeries<Row>[]` One or more series (up to 8; fold the rest into "Other").
- `x`: `string` Field used for the category / x axis.
- `area?`: `boolean` Fill under each line.
- `aria-label?`: `string` Accessible name when there is no visible title.
- `className?`: `string` Extra class names for the outermost element.
- `classNames?`: `Partial<Record<"root" | "title" | "legend" | "plot" | "tooltip" | "table", string>>` Extra class names for the component's inner parts, keyed by part name. Handy with Tailwind.
- `curved?`: `boolean` Smooth the lines. Default `true`.
- `description?`: `string` One-line summary for screen readers, e.g. "Revenue rose 40% in Q3".
- `formatX?`: `((value: unknown) => string)` Format x values for axis, tooltip and table. Default: dates by locale, others as text.
- `height?`: `number` Height in px. Width follows the container. Default 280.
- `legend?`: `boolean` Show the legend (default: when there are 2+ series).
- `showPoints?`: `boolean` Show a dot on every point (default: only the hovered one).
- `stacked?`: `boolean` Stack the series (implies `area`).
- `tableView?`: `boolean` Show a "Data table" toggle under the chart. Default `true`.
- `title?`: `ReactNode` Title shown above the chart; also its accessible name.
- `valueFormat?`: `NumberFormatOptions` Intl options for values, e.g. `{ style: 'currency', currency: 'INR', notation: 'compact' }`.
- `zeroBaseline?`: `boolean` Start the y axis at zero. Default `true` for areas, `false` for lines.

### BarChart
Compare amounts side by side, stacked or horizontally. Bars are rounded only
at their ends with a little gap between them, so they stay easy to read even
with several series.

Compare amounts across categories. Grouped or `stacked`,
vertical or `horizontal`. Thin bars with 4px rounded data ends, square to
the baseline, a 2px gap between neighbours; a per-group tooltip on hover
or keyboard (focus the chart, then arrow keys), legend toggles and a
data-table view.

Style hooks: `.sp-chart[data-kind="bar"]`, `__bar[data-active]`, `__band`.

- `data`: `Row[]` One object per point on the x axis, with a field for `x` and one for each series, e.g. `{ month: 'Jan', sales: 420 }`.
- `series`: `ChartSeries<Row>[]` One or more series (up to 8; fold the rest into "Other").
- `x`: `string` Field used for the category / x axis.
- `aria-label?`: `string` Accessible name when there is no visible title.
- `className?`: `string` Extra class names for the outermost element.
- `classNames?`: `Partial<Record<"root" | "title" | "legend" | "plot" | "tooltip" | "table", string>>` Extra class names for the component's inner parts, keyed by part name. Handy with Tailwind.
- `description?`: `string` One-line summary for screen readers, e.g. "Revenue rose 40% in Q3".
- `formatX?`: `((value: unknown) => string)` Format x values for axis, tooltip and table. Default: dates by locale, others as text.
- `height?`: `number` Height in px. Width follows the container. Default 280.
- `horizontal?`: `boolean` Bars run left to right (good for long category names).
- `legend?`: `boolean` Show the legend (default: when there are 2+ series).
- `stacked?`: `boolean` Stack the series in one bar instead of side by side.
- `tableView?`: `boolean` Show a "Data table" toggle under the chart. Default `true`.
- `title?`: `ReactNode` Title shown above the chart; also its accessible name.
- `valueFormat?`: `NumberFormatOptions` Intl options for values, e.g. `{ style: 'currency', currency: 'INR', notation: 'compact' }`.

### DonutChart
Parts of a whole, with room for a headline number in the middle. Best with a
handful of slices; the legend shows values and percentages so nothing
depends on colour alone.

Share of a whole. Slices start at 12 o'clock in data order,
separated by a 2px surface gap; the legend lists every slice with its
value and percentage so identity never depends on colour alone. Hover or
focus a slice (Tab, then ← →) for its tooltip.

Style hooks: `.sp-chart[data-kind="donut"]`, `__slice[data-active]`, `__center`.

- `data`: `DonutSlice[]` Parts of one whole. Keep it to 6 or fewer; fold the rest into "Other".
- `aria-label?`: `string` Accessible name, read by screen readers. Use it when there's no visible label.
- `centerCaption?`: `ReactNode` Small caption under the headline. Default "Total".
- `centerLabel?`: `ReactNode` Headline in the hole. Default: the total.
- `className?`: `string` Extra class names for the outermost element.
- `classNames?`: `Partial<Record<"root" | "title" | "legend" | "plot", string>>` Extra class names for the component's inner parts, keyed by part name. Handy with Tailwind.
- `size?`: `number` Diameter in px. Default 200.
- `thickness?`: `number` Ring thickness in px. Default 28.
- `title?`: `ReactNode` Heading shown above the chart, also used as its accessible name.
- `valueFormat?`: `NumberFormatOptions` Intl number format for values in the legend and tooltip, e.g. `{ style: 'currency', currency: 'INR' }`.

### Sparkline
A tiny trend line that fits in a table cell or beside a number. No axes, no
fuss, just the shape of the data and, optionally, its latest value.

A word-sized trend for tables, stat tiles and cards. No axes;
the last point is marked so the current value is easy to find. Its
accessible name states the first, last and range.

- `aria-label`: `string` What the line shows, for screen readers, e.g. "Sign-ups, last 30 days".
- `data`: `number[]` Values in order (oldest first).
- `area?`: `boolean` Fill under the line.
- `className?`: `string` Extra class names for the outermost element.
- `color?`: `string` Line colour. Default `--spark-chart-1`.
- `height?`: `number` Height in pixels. Default 32.
- `showLast?`: `boolean` Mark the last value with a dot. Default `true`.
- `width?`: `number` Width in pixels. Default 120.

## Dropdown (`dropdown`)
Pick one value from a list.

```tsx
import { Dropdown } from '@sparkwire/core';
```
Install: `npx sparkwire add dropdown` (copy source) or use the npm package. Examples and props: https://phoenix-am.github.io/spark-ui/components/dropdown

### Dropdown
A select menu that looks the part. Type to jump to an option, group long
lists under headings, and add an icon or helper text. It submits with forms
like a native select.

Pick one value from a list. The chosen option's node lights up.
Built on the Popover and ListBox base components with React Aria:
typeahead on the closed and open list, arrow keys, Home/End, Escape,
groups with headings, screen-reader announcements, and a hidden native
select so plain forms and autofill work. `Select` is the same component.

Style hooks: `.sp-dropdown[data-open][data-invalid][data-disabled]`,
`__label`, `__trigger`, `__value[data-placeholder]`, `__chevron`,
`__helper`; the list uses `.sp-popover`, `.sp-listbox` and `.sp-list-item`.

- `options`: `(DropdownOption<V> | DropdownOptionGroup<V>)[]` Options, or groups of options with a heading: `{ label: 'Asia', options: [...] }`.
- `aria-label?`: `string` Accessible name when there is no visible label.
- `className?`: `string` Extra class names for the outermost element.
- `classNames?`: `Partial<Record<"root" | "label" | "trigger" | "value" | "popover" | "option" | "helper", string>>` Extra classes for each part: root, label, trigger, value, popover, option, helper.
- `defaultValue?`: `string | number` Initial value when uncontrolled.
- `disabled?`: `boolean` Turns the control off: it can't be focused or changed, and it's announced as disabled.
- `emptyState?`: `ReactNode` Shown when there are no options. Default "No options".
- `error?`: `ReactNode` An error message, or `true` to mark the field invalid and show `helperText` as the error.
- `helperText?`: `ReactNode` Help text under the field (shown in the error colour when `error` is `true`).
- `label?`: `string` Visible label. Use `aria-label` instead if there is no visible label.
- `name?`: `string` Form field name; a hidden native select submits the value.
- `onBlur?`: `((event: FocusEvent<Element, Element>) => void)` Called when the field loses focus. Handy for validating on blur.
- `onChange?`: `((value: V) => void)` Called with the chosen option's value; its type follows the options (numbers stay numbers).
- `onFocus?`: `((event: FocusEvent<Element, Element>) => void)` Called when the field gains focus.
- `onOpenChange?`: `((open: boolean) => void)` Called when the list opens or closes.
- `placeholder?`: `string` Shown when nothing is selected. Default "Select an option".
- `required?`: `boolean` Marks the field as required: screen readers announce it and the form won't submit while it's empty.
- `size?`: `"small" | "medium" | "large"` Height 36, 46 or 54px. Default `medium`.
- `startIcon?`: `ReactNode` Icon at the start of the field.
- `value?`: `string | number | null` Controlled value (`null` for none).
- `appendIcon?`: `ReactNode` **Deprecated.** Put an `icon` on each option instead.
- `containerStyle?`: `CSSProperties` **Deprecated.** Use `classNames.root` or `className`.
- `forTeams?`: `boolean` **Deprecated.** Put `icon: <User />` on each option.
- `inputStyle?`: `CSSProperties` **Deprecated.** Use `classNames.trigger`.
- `itemStyle?`: `CSSProperties` **Deprecated.** Use `classNames.option`.
- `listContainerStyle?`: `CSSProperties` **Deprecated.** Use `classNames.popover`.
- `prependIcon?`: `ReactNode` **Deprecated.** Use `startIcon`.
- `showBorder?`: `boolean` **Deprecated.** Use `classNames` or CSS on `.sp-dropdown__trigger`.

## Combobox (`combobox`)
Type to search, then pick.

```tsx
import { Combobox } from '@sparkwire/core';
```
Install: `npx sparkwire add combobox` (copy source) or use the npm package. Examples and props: https://phoenix-am.github.io/spark-ui/components/combobox

### Combobox
A text input with suggestions, for when the list is too long to scroll.
Matching ignores case and accents, results can come from your server, and
you can allow values that aren't in the list.

Type to search a list, then pick. The field charges as you type
and the matching option lights up. Built on the InputBase, Popover and
ListBox base components with React Aria: filtering that ignores case and
accents, arrow keys, Enter to pick, Escape to close or clear, groups,
free entry, server-side search, and screen-reader announcements of
result counts.

Style hooks: `.sp-combobox[data-open][data-invalid][data-disabled][data-loading]`,
`__label`, `__helper`, `__spinner`; the field is `.sp-input-base`, the
list `.sp-popover`, `.sp-listbox` and `.sp-list-item`.

- `options`: `(ComboboxOption<V> | ComboboxOptionGroup<V>)[]` Options, or groups of options with a heading.
- `allowsCustomValue?`: `boolean` Keep typed text that matches no option (free entry, e.g. tags or a new city).
- `aria-label?`: `string` Accessible name when there is no visible label.
- `className?`: `string` Extra class names for the outermost element.
- `classNames?`: `Partial<Record<"input" | "root" | "label" | "field" | "popover" | "option" | "helper", string>>` Extra classes for each part: root, label, field, input, popover, option, helper.
- `clearable?`: `boolean` Show a clear button when there is text. Default `true`.
- `defaultInputValue?`: `string` Initial text in the input when uncontrolled.
- `defaultValue?`: `string | number` Initial selected value when uncontrolled.
- `disabled?`: `boolean` Turns the control off: it can't be focused or changed, and it's announced as disabled.
- `emptyState?`: `ReactNode` Shown when nothing matches. Default "No results".
- `error?`: `ReactNode` An error message, or `true` to mark the field invalid and show `helperText` as the error.
- `filter?`: `false | "contains" | "startsWith"` How options are matched to the typed text: `contains` (default), `startsWith`, or `false` when you filter yourself (e.g. server search). Matching ignores case and accents.
- `helperText?`: `ReactNode` Help text under the field (shown in the error colour when `error` is `true`).
- `inputValue?`: `string` Controlled text in the input.
- `label?`: `string` Visible label. Use `aria-label` instead if there is no visible label.
- `loading?`: `boolean` Show a loading indicator, e.g. while fetching options.
- `loadingText?`: `ReactNode` Text shown in the list while `loading`. Default "Loading…".
- `menuTrigger?`: `"input" | "focus" | "manual"` When the list opens: on typing (`input`, default), on focus, or only with the button or arrow keys (`manual`).
- `name?`: `string` Form field name. Submits the selected value (or the typed text with `allowsCustomValue`).
- `onChange?`: `((value: V | null) => void)` Called with the chosen option's value, or `null` when cleared.
- `onInputChange?`: `((text: string) => void)` Called as the user types; use it to fetch options from a server (with `filter={false}`).
- `placeholder?`: `string` Placeholder text in the input.
- `required?`: `boolean` Marks the field as required: screen readers announce it and the form won't submit while it's empty.
- `size?`: `"small" | "medium" | "large"` Height 36, 46 or 54px. Default `medium`.
- `startIcon?`: `ReactNode` Icon at the start of the field, e.g. a search icon.
- `value?`: `string | number | null` Controlled selected value (`null` for none).

## DatePicker (`date-picker`)
DatePicker, DateRangePicker, Calendar and RangeCalendar: typed entry, presets, date rules, locales and calendar systems.

```tsx
import { DatePicker, Segment, DateRangePicker, Calendar, RangeCalendar } from '@sparkwire/core';
```
Install: `npx sparkwire add date-picker` (copy source) or use the npm package. Examples and props: https://phoenix-am.github.io/spark-ui/components/date-picker

### DatePicker
Pick a date by typing it, stepping through each part with the arrow keys, or
choosing from a calendar. Add presets like “Tomorrow” or “+1 week”, block
weekends or past dates, and it formats for the user's locale.

Type a date or pick it from a calendar. The field lights up
while the calendar is open, and the picked day is a lit node with a spark.
Behaviour comes from React Aria: segment-by-segment typing in the
locale's order (DD/MM/YYYY in India, MM/DD/YYYY in the US), arrow keys to
adjust a segment, right-to-left layouts, other calendar systems, and a
dialog popover that restores focus.

Style hooks: `.sp-date-picker[data-open][data-invalid][data-disabled]`,
`__label`, `__control`, `.sp-date-field`, `__segment[data-placeholder]`,
`__trigger`, `__clear`, `__helper`, `__popover`.

- `aria-label?`: `string` Accessible name when there is no visible label.
- `calendar?`: `CalendarSystem` Calendar system to display, e.g. `indian` (Saka), `islamic-umalqura`, `buddhist`. Values stay JS Dates.
- `calendarClassNames?`: `Partial<Record<CalendarSlot, string>>` Extra classes for the calendar's parts (header, day, preset…).
- `className?`: `string` Extra class names for the outermost element.
- `classNames?`: `Partial<Record<"root" | "label" | "control" | "field" | "trigger" | "popover" | "helper", string>>` Extra classes for each part: root, label, control, field, trigger, popover, helper.
- `clearable?`: `boolean` Show a clear button when a date is set. Default `true`.
- `defaultValue?`: `Date | null` Initial value when uncontrolled.
- `disabled?`: `boolean` Turns the control off: it can't be focused or changed, and it's announced as disabled.
- `disabledDates?`: `Date[]` Days that can't be picked, e.g. holidays or booked days.
- `enabledDates?`: `Date[]` If set, only these days can be picked, e.g. open appointment slots.
- `error?`: `boolean` Marks the field invalid.
- `firstDayOfWeek?`: `"sun" | "mon" | "tue" | "wed" | "thu" | "fri" | "sat"` First day of the week. Defaults to the locale's convention.
- `helperText?`: `ReactNode` Help text under the field (or the error message when `error` is set).
- `isDateDisabled?`: `((date: Date) => boolean)` Return `true` for days that can't be picked, e.g. weekends. Combines with the lists above.
- `label?`: `ReactNode` Visible label above the field.
- `locale?`: `string` BCP 47 locale for names, digits and direction. Defaults to SparkProvider's or the browser's.
- `max?`: `Date` Latest selectable day.
- `min?`: `Date` Earliest selectable day.
- `name?`: `string` Name for a hidden input carrying the ISO date (YYYY-MM-DD), for plain forms.
- `onChange?`: `((date: Date | null) => void)` Called with the picked or typed date, or `null` when cleared.
- `presets?`: `(DatePreset | DatePresetName)[]` Shortcut buttons under the calendar, replacing the Today button. Short names (`'today'`, `'tomorrow'`, `'+7d'`, `'+1m'`, `'-1y'`) or your own `{ label, value }` where value is a Date or a function returning one.
- `renderDay?`: `((date: Date, info: DayRenderInfo) => ReactNode)` Custom content for a day cell, e.g. a price or an event dot under the number.
- `required?`: `boolean` Marks the date as required for form submission.
- `showToday?`: `boolean` Show the Today button. Default `true` for Calendar, `false` for RangeCalendar. Ignored when `presets` is set.
- `size?`: `"small" | "medium" | "large"` Default `medium`.
- `todayLabel?`: `string` Label for the Today button, for other languages.
- `value?`: `Date | null` Controlled value; `null` for no date.
- `visibleMonths?`: `number` Months shown side by side. Default 1.
- `format?`: `DateTimeFormatOptions` **Deprecated.** The field now shows editable segments in the locale's order.
- `placeholder?`: `string` **Deprecated.** The field now shows editable segments in the locale's order.
- `weekStartsOn?`: `0 | 1 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5 | 6` **Deprecated.** Use `firstDayOfWeek`. 0 = Sunday, 1 = Monday.

### Segment
One editable part of a date or time field, such as the day or the hour. You
won't usually use it directly.

- `segment`: `DateSegment` The date part this segment edits (day, month, year, hour…). Supplied by React Aria.
- `state`: `DateFieldState` The date field's state. Supplied by the parent field.

### DateRangePicker
Choose a start and an end date in one go, with two months side by side and
presets like “This month” or “Last 30 days”.

Type or pick a start and an end date; current flows
between them in the calendar. Two months side by side, shortcut buttons
(`presets`) under the calendar, and full control over which days can be
picked. Behaviour comes from React Aria: typed entry in the locale's order,
hover preview of the range, right-to-left, calendar systems.

Style hooks: `.sp-date-picker.sp-date-range-picker[data-open][data-invalid]`,
`__control`, `.sp-date-field`, `__dash`, `__trigger`, `__clear`, `__popover`.

- `allowsNonContiguousRanges?`: `boolean` Allow ranges that cross unavailable days. Default `false`.
- `aria-label?`: `string` Accessible name when there is no visible label.
- `calendar?`: `CalendarSystem` Calendar system to display, e.g. `indian` (Saka), `islamic-umalqura`, `buddhist`. Values stay JS Dates.
- `calendarClassNames?`: `Partial<Record<CalendarSlot, string>>` Extra classes for the calendar's parts.
- `className?`: `string` Extra class names for the outermost element.
- `classNames?`: `Partial<Record<"root" | "label" | "control" | "field" | "trigger" | "popover" | "helper", string>>` Extra classes for each part: root, label, control, field, trigger, popover, helper.
- `clearable?`: `boolean` Show a clear button when a range is set. Default `true`.
- `defaultValue?`: `DateRange | null` Initial range when uncontrolled.
- `disabled?`: `boolean` Turns the control off: it can't be focused or changed, and it's announced as disabled.
- `disabledDates?`: `Date[]` Days that can't be picked, e.g. holidays or booked days.
- `enabledDates?`: `Date[]` If set, only these days can be picked, e.g. open appointment slots.
- `endName?`: `string` Hidden input with the end date (ISO), e.g. `checkOut`.
- `error?`: `boolean` Shows the field in its error state. Pair it with `helperText`.
- `firstDayOfWeek?`: `"sun" | "mon" | "tue" | "wed" | "thu" | "fri" | "sat"` First day of the week. Defaults to the locale's convention.
- `helperText?`: `ReactNode` Help text under the field (or the error message when `error` is set).
- `isDateDisabled?`: `((date: Date) => boolean)` Return `true` for days that can't be picked, e.g. weekends. Combines with the lists above.
- `label?`: `ReactNode` Visible label above the field.
- `locale?`: `string` BCP 47 locale for names, digits and direction. Defaults to SparkProvider's or the browser's.
- `max?`: `Date` Latest selectable day.
- `min?`: `Date` Earliest selectable day.
- `name?`: `string` One hidden input with an ISO interval, e.g. `2026-12-01/2026-12-07`.
- `onChange?`: `((range: DateRange | null) => void)` Called with the picked or typed range, or `null` when cleared.
- `presets?`: `(RangePreset | RangePresetName)[]` Shortcut buttons under the calendar. Short names (`'+7d'` next 7 days, `'-30d'` last 30 days, `'thisWeek'`, `'thisMonth'`, `'thisYear'`, `'today'`) or your own `{ label, value }`.
- `renderDay?`: `((date: Date, info: DayRenderInfo) => ReactNode)` Custom content for a day cell, e.g. a price or an event dot under the number.
- `required?`: `boolean` Marks the field as required: screen readers announce it and the form won't submit while it's empty.
- `size?`: `"small" | "medium" | "large"` Default `medium`.
- `startName?`: `string` Hidden input with the start date (ISO), e.g. `checkIn`.
- `value?`: `DateRange | null` Controlled range; `null` for none.
- `visibleMonths?`: `number` Months shown in the popover. Default 2.
- `weekStartsOn?`: `0 | 1 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5 | 6` **Deprecated.** Use `firstDayOfWeek`. 0 = Sunday, 1 = Monday.

### Calendar
The month grid on its own, for when you want a calendar on the page rather
than in a popover.

A month grid. The selected day is a lit node, today is a ring,
and picking a day throws a spark. Shortcut buttons (`presets`) sit under
the grid. Behaviour comes from React Aria: arrows, Page Up/Down (Shift for
years), Home/End, right-to-left mirroring, localized names and digits,
other calendar systems, and announcements when the month changes.

Style hooks: `.sp-calendar`, `__header`, `__title`, `__nav`, `__months`,
`__grid`, `__weekday`, `__day` with `[data-selected]`, `[data-today]`,
`[data-unavailable]`, `[data-outside]`, `[data-focus-visible]`,
`__footer`, `__preset[data-active]`. Add classes with `classNames`.

- `aria-label?`: `string` Accessible name for the calendar.
- `autoFocus?`: `boolean` Move keyboard focus into the grid when the calendar mounts.
- `calendar?`: `CalendarSystem` Calendar system to display, e.g. `indian` (Saka), `islamic-umalqura`, `buddhist`. Values stay JS Dates.
- `className?`: `string` Extra class names for the outermost element.
- `classNames?`: `Partial<Record<CalendarSlot, string>>` Extra classes for each part.
- `defaultValue?`: `Date | null` Initial selected day when uncontrolled.
- `disabledDates?`: `Date[]` Days that can't be picked, e.g. holidays or booked days.
- `enabledDates?`: `Date[]` If set, only these days can be picked, e.g. open appointment slots.
- `firstDayOfWeek?`: `"sun" | "mon" | "tue" | "wed" | "thu" | "fri" | "sat"` First day of the week. Defaults to the locale's convention.
- `isDateDisabled?`: `((date: Date) => boolean)` Return `true` for days that can't be picked, e.g. weekends. Combines with the lists above.
- `locale?`: `string` BCP 47 locale for names, digits and direction. Defaults to SparkProvider's or the browser's.
- `max?`: `Date` Latest selectable day.
- `min?`: `Date` Earliest selectable day.
- `onChange?`: `((date: Date) => void)` Called with the picked day.
- `onEscape?`: `(() => void)` Called on Escape, so a custom popover can close.
- `presets?`: `(DatePreset | DatePresetName)[]` Shortcut buttons under the calendar, replacing the Today button. Short names (`'today'`, `'tomorrow'`, `'+7d'`, `'+1m'`, `'-1y'`) or your own `{ label, value }` where value is a Date or a function returning one.
- `renderDay?`: `((date: Date, info: DayRenderInfo) => ReactNode)` Custom content for a day cell, e.g. a price or an event dot under the number.
- `showToday?`: `boolean` Show the Today button. Default `true` for Calendar, `false` for RangeCalendar. Ignored when `presets` is set.
- `todayLabel?`: `string` Label for the Today button, for other languages.
- `value?`: `Date | null` The selected day.
- `visibleMonths?`: `number` Months shown side by side. Default 1.
- `weekStartsOn?`: `0 | 1 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5 | 6` **Deprecated.** Use `firstDayOfWeek`. 0 = Sunday, 1 = Monday.

### RangeCalendar
A calendar for picking a range of dates, without the input field around it.

Pick a start and an end day; current flows between them.
Hovering after the first click previews the range. Shows two months with
`visibleMonths={2}`. Shortcut buttons (`presets`) sit under the grid.

Style hooks: as Calendar, plus `__day[data-range-start][data-range-end][data-in-range]`.

- `allowsNonContiguousRanges?`: `boolean` Allow ranges that cross unavailable days. Default `false`.
- `aria-label?`: `string` Accessible name for the calendar.
- `autoFocus?`: `boolean` Move keyboard focus into the grid when the calendar mounts.
- `calendar?`: `CalendarSystem` Calendar system to display, e.g. `indian` (Saka), `islamic-umalqura`, `buddhist`. Values stay JS Dates.
- `className?`: `string` Extra class names for the outermost element.
- `classNames?`: `Partial<Record<CalendarSlot, string>>` Extra classes for each part.
- `defaultValue?`: `DateRange | null` Initial range when uncontrolled.
- `disabledDates?`: `Date[]` Days that can't be picked, e.g. holidays or booked days.
- `enabledDates?`: `Date[]` If set, only these days can be picked, e.g. open appointment slots.
- `firstDayOfWeek?`: `"sun" | "mon" | "tue" | "wed" | "thu" | "fri" | "sat"` First day of the week. Defaults to the locale's convention.
- `isDateDisabled?`: `((date: Date) => boolean)` Return `true` for days that can't be picked, e.g. weekends. Combines with the lists above.
- `locale?`: `string` BCP 47 locale for names, digits and direction. Defaults to SparkProvider's or the browser's.
- `max?`: `Date` Latest selectable day.
- `min?`: `Date` Earliest selectable day.
- `onChange?`: `((range: DateRange) => void)` Called with the picked range once both ends are chosen.
- `onEscape?`: `(() => void)` Called on Escape, so a custom popover can close.
- `presets?`: `(RangePreset | RangePresetName)[]` Shortcut buttons under the calendar. Short names (`'+7d'` next 7 days, `'-30d'` last 30 days, `'thisWeek'`, `'thisMonth'`, `'thisYear'`, `'today'`) or your own `{ label, value }`.
- `renderDay?`: `((date: Date, info: DayRenderInfo) => ReactNode)` Custom content for a day cell, e.g. a price or an event dot under the number.
- `showToday?`: `boolean` Show the Today button. Default `true` for Calendar, `false` for RangeCalendar. Ignored when `presets` is set.
- `todayLabel?`: `string` Label for the Today button, for other languages.
- `value?`: `DateRange | null` The selected range.
- `visibleMonths?`: `number` Months shown side by side. Default 1.
- `weekStartsOn?`: `0 | 1 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5 | 6` **Deprecated.** Use `firstDayOfWeek`. 0 = Sunday, 1 = Monday.

## DataTable (`data-table`)
Sort, search, filter, page and select rows; responsive div grid, no table library.

```tsx
import { DataTable } from '@sparkwire/core';
```
Install: `npx sparkwire add data-table` (copy source) or use the npm package. Examples and props: https://phoenix-am.github.io/spark-ui/components/data-table

### DataTable
A full data grid without a table library. Sort, search, filter, page and
select rows; resize and pin columns; expand rows for details; edit cells in
place; and scroll through thousands of rows smoothly. On narrow screens rows
turn into readable cards.

Sort, search, filter, page and select rows; resize and pin
columns, expand rows, edit cells in place, and virtualise thousands of
rows. Built from divs on a CSS grid (like MUI's Data Grid), so it adapts
to its container: in narrow spaces rows become labelled cards. The table
logic is Sparkwire's own (`useDataTable`); React Aria supplies grid
keyboard navigation and screen-reader semantics.

Keyboard: arrows move between cells, Home/End and Page Up/Down jump,
Space selects a row, Enter activates it (or edits an editable cell; F2
too), Shift+click sorts by more than one column. Tab from a resizable
column header reaches its resize handle, which takes the arrow keys.

Style hooks: `.sp-data-table[data-density][data-striped][data-responsive][data-virtual]`,
`__toolbar`, `__grid[aria-busy]`, `__header`, `__column[data-sorted][data-sortable][data-pinned]`,
`__resizer`, `__row[data-selected][data-expanded]`, `__cell[data-align][data-pinned][data-editing]`,
`__expander`, `__detail`, `__editor`, `__footer`.

- `columns`: `DataTableColumn<RowT>[]` What to show, in order. Each column has a `key` (the field to read), a `header`, and options like `sortable`, `width`, `cell`, `editable` or `pin`.
- `data`: `RowT[]` The rows: an array of objects. Each needs a unique `id`, or pass `getRowKey`.
- `aria-label?`: `string` Accessible name; describe what the table lists.
- `aria-labelledby?`: `string` Id of an element whose text names this component, instead of `aria-label`.
- `bulkActions?`: `((rows: RowT[]) => ReactNode)` Actions shown when rows are selected, e.g. a delete button. Receives the selected rows.
- `className?`: `string` Extra class names for the outermost element.
- `classNames?`: `Partial<Record<"root" | "toolbar" | "grid" | "header" | "columnHeader" | "row" | "cell" | "footer", string>>` Extra classes for each part.
- `columnWidths?`: `Record<string, number>` Column widths in px by column key (controlled).
- `defaultColumnWidths?`: `Record<string, number>` Starting widths in pixels, by column key, when the table manages resizing itself.
- `defaultExpandedKeys?`: `Iterable<string>` Rows that start expanded, by key.
- `defaultFilters?`: `Record<string, unknown>` Starting filter values, by column key.
- `defaultPage?`: `number` Starting page (0-based) when the table manages paging itself.
- `defaultPageSize?`: `number` Starting rows per page. Default 10, or all rows with `virtualize`.
- `defaultSearch?`: `string` Starting text in the search box.
- `defaultSelectedKeys?`: `Iterable<string>` Rows that start selected, by key.
- `defaultSort?`: `SortRule[]` Starting sort, e.g. `[{ column: 'updated', direction: 'descending' }]`. Add more entries to sort by several columns.
- `density?`: `"compact" | "normal" | "comfortable"` Row height. Default `normal`.
- `emptyState?`: `ReactNode` Shown when there are no rows. Default "No results".
- `expandedKeys?`: `Set<string>` Expanded row keys (controlled).
- `filters?`: `Record<string, unknown>` Controlled per-column filter values, keyed by column.
- `getRowKey?`: `((row: RowT, index: number) => string)` Stable id for each row. Default: `row.id`, then the index.
- `loading?`: `boolean` Show placeholder rows while data loads.
- `manual?`: `boolean` Server-side mode: you sort, filter and page the data yourself (e.g. in an API call) and pass the current page as `data` with the total `rowCount`.
- `maxHeight?`: `string | number` Fix the height and scroll the body under a sticky header, e.g. `400`.
- `onCellEdit?`: `((row: RowT, columnKey: string, value: unknown) => void)` Save an edited cell (columns with `editable`). Update your data here; the table shows what `data` holds.
- `onColumnResize?`: `((key: string, width: number) => void)` Called when a resize ends, with the column key and its new width.
- `onExpandedChange?`: `((keys: Set<string>) => void)` Called with the set of expanded row keys whenever a row opens or closes.
- `onFiltersChange?`: `((filters: Record<string, unknown>) => void)` Called with all filter values whenever one changes. Use it to filter on your server.
- `onPageChange?`: `((page: number) => void)` Called with the new page index (0-based).
- `onPageSizeChange?`: `((size: number) => void)` Called with the new number of rows per page.
- `onRowAction?`: `((row: RowT, key: string) => void)` Called when a row is activated (click, or Enter on the row).
- `onSearchChange?`: `((search: string) => void)` Called with the search text as it's typed. Use it to search on your server.
- `onSelectionChange?`: `((keys: Set<string>) => void)` Called with the set of selected row keys, across all pages.
- `onSortChange?`: `((sort: SortRule[]) => void)` Called with the new sort rules when a header is clicked.
- `page?`: `number` Controlled page (0-based).
- `pageSize?`: `number` Rows per page; `0` turns paging off. Default 10.
- `pageSizeOptions?`: `number[]` Page sizes to offer. Default `[10, 25, 50]`. Pass `[]` to hide the picker.
- `renderExpanded?`: `((row: RowT) => ReactNode)` Content shown under a row when it's expanded; adds an expand button to each row.
- `resizableColumns?`: `boolean` Let people resize every column (drag its edge, or Tab to the edge and use the arrow keys). Columns can also opt in with `resizable`.
- `responsive?`: `"stack" | "scroll"` In a narrow container: `stack` (default) turns rows into labelled cards; `scroll` keeps the grid and scrolls sideways.
- `rowCount?`: `number` Total rows on the server, for paging in `manual` mode.
- `rowHeight?`: `number` Row height in px for `virtualize`. Default from `density`: 36, 44 or 52.
- `search?`: `string` Controlled search text (matches any searchable column).
- `searchable?`: `boolean` Show a search box over the table.
- `searchPlaceholder?`: `string` Placeholder for the search box.
- `selectedKeys?`: `Set<string>` Controlled selected row keys.
- `selectionMode?`: `"none" | "single" | "multiple"` `multiple` adds checkboxes; `single` selects one row. Default `none`.
- `sort?`: `SortRule[]` Controlled sort rules (first wins).
- `stackBelow?`: `number` Container width (px) below which rows stack. Default 640.
- `striped?`: `boolean` Shade every other row.
- `toolbar?`: `ReactNode` Extra content in the toolbar, e.g. filter dropdowns or an export button.
- `virtualize?`: `boolean` Render only the rows in view, for thousands of rows. Needs `maxHeight`; paging is off unless you set a page size, rows have a fixed height (`rowHeight`), and rows don't stack or expand.

## CommandPalette (`command-palette`)
A ⌘K launcher: search commands and pages, run with the keyboard.

```tsx
import { CommandPalette } from '@sparkwire/core';
```
Install: `npx sparkwire add command-palette` (copy source) or use the npm package. Examples and props: https://phoenix-am.github.io/spark-ui/components/command-palette

### CommandPalette
One keyboard shortcut (⌘K or Ctrl+K) to reach anything in your app: pages,
actions, settings. It searches as you type, groups results, and shows
shortcuts. This site's search is built with it.

A ⌘K launcher. Type to find a command or page; arrows move
the lit node, Enter runs it, Escape closes. Focus stays in the search box
(ARIA combobox with an active option), the dialog traps focus and returns
it when closed. Groups, keywords, icons, shortcuts, links and async
results. Built on the Overlay and InputBase base components and the
shared list-item look.

Style hooks: `.sp-command`, `__panel`, `__input`, `__list`, `__group`,
`__heading`, `.sp-list-item[data-focused]`, `__empty`, `__toolbar`, `__body`,
`__preview`, `__footer`.

- `items`: `(Command | CommandGroup)[]` Commands, or groups of commands with a heading.
- `aria-label?`: `string` Accessible name for the dialog. Default "Command palette".
- `className?`: `string` Extra class names for the outermost element.
- `classNames?`: `Partial<Record<"panel" | "input" | "toolbar" | "list" | "group" | "item" | "preview" | "footer", string>>` Extra classes for each part: panel, input, toolbar, list, group, item, preview, footer.
- `closeOnSelect?`: `boolean` Close after a command runs. Default `true`.
- `defaultOpen?`: `boolean` Start open, when the palette manages its own state.
- `emptyState?`: `ReactNode` Shown when nothing matches. Default "No results".
- `filter?`: `boolean` Match commands to the search yourself. Default `true` (case- and accent-insensitive, best matches first).
- `hideFooter?`: `boolean` Hide the keyboard hints at the bottom.
- `hotkey?`: `string | false` Keyboard shortcut that opens and closes the palette. Default `mod+k` (⌘K on Mac, Ctrl+K elsewhere). `false` to turn off.
- `loading?`: `boolean` Show a loading line, e.g. while fetching.
- `onOpenChange?`: `((open: boolean) => void)` Called with `true` or `false` when the palette opens or closes, including from the hotkey.
- `onSearchChange?`: `((search: string) => void)` Called with the search text, e.g. to fetch results from a server (with `filter={false}`).
- `onSelect?`: `((command: Command) => void)` Called with the chosen command, after its own `onSelect`.
- `open?`: `boolean` Controlled open state.
- `placeholder?`: `string` Hint in the search box. Default “Type a command or search…”.
- `preview?`: `((command: Command) => ReactNode)` A pane beside the results that shows more about the highlighted command: a live example, a description, actions. Called with `undefined` when nothing is highlighted. The panel widens to make room, and the pane is hidden on narrow screens.
- `toolbar?`: `ReactNode` A row under the search box, e.g. tabs that narrow what the search covers.

## Menu (`menu`)
Actions behind a button, with submenus.

```tsx
import { Menu } from '@sparkwire/core';
```
Install: `npx sparkwire add menu` (copy source) or use the npm package. Examples and props: https://phoenix-am.github.io/spark-ui/components/menu

### Menu
A list of actions behind a button, like “Rename” and “Delete”. Supports
sections, icons, descriptions, nested submenus, and single or multiple
selection for things like sort order.

A list of actions behind a button (Edit, Duplicate, Delete). Not for
picking a value: use Dropdown for that. Built on the Popover base and the
shared list-item look, with React Aria's menu behaviour: arrow keys,
typeahead, Enter/Space to run, Escape to close, submenus that open with
the right arrow (left in right-to-left), sections, links, checkable items,
and focus returning to the trigger.

Style hooks: `.sp-menu`, `.sp-list-item[data-focused][data-danger][data-disabled][data-open]`,
`__end` (shortcut), `__chevron`, `__check`; trigger `.sp-menu-trigger`.

- `items`: `MenuEntry[]` Items, sections (`{ title, items }`) and submenus (`items` on an item).
- `aria-label?`: `string` Accessible name for the menu. Defaults to the trigger's text.
- `className?`: `string` Extra class names for the outermost element.
